title: Borrowing Struct Fields
goal: Understand how Rust borrows individual struct fields versus borrowing &mut self.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 2 Morning: Borrow Checking

sections.text: Rust's borrow checker understands struct fields. You can borrow two different fields of a struct at the same time, even if one borrow is mutable.

sections.caption: Borrowing p.name leaves p.hp available for mutation.

sections.text: However, calling a method that takes `&mut self` borrows the entire struct mutably. While that method borrow is active, no field of the struct can be read or borrowed.

sections.caption: &mut self borrows the entire struct, conflicting with name_ref.

sections.text: To fix this conflict, finish using the field reference before calling the method, or access the fields directly instead of calling `&mut self` methods.

explanation: Understand how Rust borrows individual struct fields versus borrowing &mut self.
